title: India’s First TSMC 12nm Edge AI Chip Marks a Semiconductor Milestone
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

Indian semiconductor startup Netrasemi has achieved a significant milestone with the development of its A2000, an indigenously designed TSMC 12nm edge artificial intelligence system-on-chip (SoC).

Based in Kerala and backed by investors including Zoho and Unicorn India Ventures, Netrasemi successfully completed silicon testing and announced production readiness in May 2026. Customer evaluations are underway, with commercial availability targeted for mid-2027.

Manufactured using TSMC’s 12nm process technology, the A2000 integrates internally developed neural processing, computer vision, image processing, video and security engines.

Unlike cloud-based AI solutions, edge AI processors perform computations locally within devices, reducing latency, network bandwidth requirements and dependence on cloud infrastructure.

The A2000 targets several rapidly growing markets:

Intelligent cameras and video processing.
Industrial automation and robotics.
Internet of Things (IoT) devices.
Automotive applications.
Intelligent edge computing systems.
Netrasemi has also developed the R1000 AI-enabled microcontroller and is working on the A4000, a more advanced edge AI server processor.

The company's development efforts have benefited from India’s Design Linked Incentive (DLI) scheme, which supports domestic semiconductor design capabilities and intellectual property development.

Why it Matters:
India has historically been a major global semiconductor engineering hub, but relatively few Indian companies have developed and commercialized their own advanced semiconductor products.

The A2000 demonstrates India’s growing ability to move beyond semiconductor design services toward proprietary chip architectures and commercially viable silicon.

Although the chip is manufactured overseas, its domestic design and intellectual property development represent important steps toward greater technological independence.

Edge AI presents a substantial opportunity for Indian semiconductor companies to compete globally without directly challenging Nvidia in high-end AI training accelerators.

India’s semiconductor ambitions are increasingly moving from engineering talent and manufacturing incentives toward homegrown intellectual property, product innovation and commercial silicon.
